subtext: Built, rebuilt and tested by engineers who work on BMW engines every day.
Here's our practical view of the S63 across all 6 model applications.

columns.title: APPLICATIONS WE SEE:
columns.body: The S63 is BMW M's twin-turbo V8, fitted across the M5, M6, M8, X5 M and X6 M — a relatively contained application set compared to the B58's 14-model spread, but one that covers a broad power and weight range.

columns.title: WHAT WE REPLACE:
columns.body: Timing chain components, bearings, gaskets and seals — including valve seals, given this engine's hot-vee architecture — are replaced as standard on every S63 rebuild.

columns.title: KNOWN ISSUES:
columns.body: The S63's hot-vee design — with the turbochargers positioned in the V between the cylinder banks — means heat-related component degradation is a factor we account for, particularly valve seal wear and coolant system component wear. Timing chain stretch has also been documented across some applications. None of these are universal or inevitable — they're specific wear mechanisms we inspect for during a rebuild, and we replace components where required. We don't treat this engine as having a single catastrophic failure mode; diagnosis is required to establish whether an engine needs repair, rebuild or replacement.
